data.description:
## Report

`rebar transition <id> in_progress closed` can print a lock-timeout error to stderr **with exit code 0**, roughly 60s AFTER the close is already durably committed — and silently downgrade the ticket to closed-WITHOUT-signature.

Observed in the field: an agent reported its final `rebar transition` failed with a lock error, but re-reading showed the transition had LANDED.

## Mechanism

The STATUS event commits at `txn.py:299` and the lock releases at `txn.py:311`. The command then performs up to FIVE more lock acquisitions. The one that surfaces:

```
transition_close.py:433  sign_completion_verdict(...)
  signing.py:574         append_event(resolved, "SIGNATURE", ...)
  _seam.py:521           write_and_push(...)
  event_append.py:382    with _lock.write_lock(tracker, dual_window=True)   # 60s budget
  lock.py:704/709        raise LockTimeout(...)
  _seam.py:528-533       -> CommandError(str(exc), 1)
  signing.py:582-583     -> SigningError
  transition_close.py:434 except SigningError
  transition_close.py:440 stderr: "Warning: closed <id> WITHOUT a completion signature — flock: ..."
```

Exit code is 0. The other post-write acquisitions are swallowed entirely: `_apply_caused_by` (`transition_close.py:255`), the force-close audit comment (`:473`), compact-on-close (`:131` StringIO + `:133`), push merge recovery (`push.py:379`, `:735`).

A second variant returns exit 1 after a DIFFERENT ticket landed: the parent-first cascade (`transition.py:399`, `claim.py:241`) commits and pushes the parent, then the child acquisition times out.

## Why it matters beyond cosmetics

The ticket ends up **closed without a completion signature**, which reads as a bypassed gate. The caller cannot tell from the exit code that anything was lost, and the printed text describes a failure of the very operation that in fact succeeded.

Note: bug royal-weariless-zebrafish adds bounded retry at `event_append.py:382`, which makes the signature append far more likely to survive contention — that MITIGATES this but does not fix the reporting shape.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A close whose completion-signature append fails does not exit 0 while reporting an error, verified by a test asserting the exit code reflects the signature outcome
- [ ] The message distinguishes "the close landed, the signature did not" from "the close failed", verified by asserting the stderr text
- [ ] The closed-without-signature state is detectable by a later reader, verified by a test
data.title: transition close reports a lock error with exit 0 after the close landed, silently dropping the completion signature
